## 3. The evidence that moved it







**Simple beats complex, in print, in March 2024.** [38428432](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38428432/) (*Cell Syst*):
convolutions are competitive with transformers for protein sequence pretraining.
This corpus has dated the simple-baselines-beat-deep-models finding twice — first
to 2026, then, after the 2025 backfill, to June 2025. It is here, in a tracked
journal, in March 2024. The correction is now the fourth of its kind and the
pattern is no longer about any individual claim.

**One laboratory ships two pathology foundation models back to back.**
[38504018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38504018/) is UNI, a general-purpose self-supervised model pretrained on
more than 100 million tiles from over 100,000 diagnostic slides across 20 tissue
types and evaluated on 34 tasks. [38504017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38504017/) is CONCH, a visual-language
model trained on 1.17 million image-caption pairs and state of the art across 14
benchmarks. Both are in the same issue of *Nature Medicine*, both are real, and
both card `supports` — two distinct models with distinct evaluations. What they
are not is two groups: they share a senior author and most of their author list.
Read them as one group's release of a pair of models, which is a claim about that
group's capability and about how far the framing has travelled in imaging, and
not as replication.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This paragraph argued that "independent convergence in the same issue is the
    strongest evidence grade available from literature alone". The convergence
    was not independent. The inference behind it — same journal, same month,
    therefore different laboratories — is the one this corpus reaches for most
    often, and it fails silently whenever a laboratory publishes back-to-back,
    because nothing in either title reveals the shared authorship. The stances
    are unchanged; the pair is one piece of evidence, not two.

**A neurotransmitter as the shared currency, made explicit.** [38489352](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38489352/)
(*Sci Immunol*): gut bacteria-derived **serotonin** promotes immune tolerance in
early life. The `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` claim asserts that
neurotransmitters are the currency between the neural, microbial and lymphoid
arms. This is that assertion as a title, twenty months before the corpus opened
the thread.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[38200243](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38200243/) (*Nat Cancer*): SIRPα on tumour-associated myeloid cells
restrains antitumour immunity **independent of its interaction with CD47**. The
don't-eat-me axis that the entire CD47 clinical programme was built on is not the
operative mechanism. In December 2025 this corpus reads two *Nature Immunology*
papers relocating CD47's function as a "mechanistic post-mortem" arriving five
months after the phase 3 failures. The post-mortem was published twenty-one
months *before* them.

[38418879](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38418879/) (*Nature*): anti-TIGIT antibody improves PD-L1 blockade through
myeloid and Treg cells — TIGIT's mechanism reassigned away from the
T-cell-intrinsic model its clinical programme assumed, two years before
SKYSCRAPER-01 reads out negative in July 2026.

[38096462](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38096462/) (*JCO*): four additional doses of PEG-L-asparaginase during
consolidation **do not** improve outcome and **increase** toxicity in high-risk
ALL, randomised — no difference in end-of-consolidation MRD or five-year
event-free survival, and adverse reactions in 22.2% against 8.9%. A clean
negative escalation trial, and it lands on no tracked thread. It was carded on
`clinical-practice`, whose claim is that meetings lead journals; this is a
journal readout that says nothing about a meeting, and all eight of that thread's
cards were the same mistake — scoring whether the clinical advice went up or
down instead of scoring the thread's actual claim. The card keeps its stance and
has no thread.

### (b) Method credibility

[38416482](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38416482/) (*JAMA*): blind spots, shortcuts and automation bias in AI
clinical models. Read with [38504018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38504018/) and [38504017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38504017/) above — the
enthusiasm and its audit are again in the same month, not separated by the
interval this corpus once recorded.
